2607.09099.title: L-MAD: A Systematic Evaluation of Multi-Agent Debate Structures in Legal Reasoning
2607.09099.paper_summary: While multi-agent debate (MAD) frameworks have shown significant potential in general reasoning, their effectiveness in highly structured, knowledge-heavy legal domains remains under-explored. In this work, we introduce the Legal Multi-Agent Debate (L-MAD) framework to systematically evaluate different debate structures and aggregation methods within Legal Textual Entailment. By assigning distinct expert personas to multiple agents, L-MAD improves upon strong single-agent baselines by up to 8\%. Furthermore, analyzing how debate scales reveals a clear trade-off: increasing the agent population reduces inconsistency and improves accuracy, whereas extending discussion rounds induces a detrimental \textit{over-deliberation drift} where agents reinforce each other's mistakes. Ultimately, our findings outline the practical boundaries and safety margins of deploying collaborative multi-agent systems in high-stakes legal reasoning environments.
2607.09099.paper_summary_zh: 雖然多代理辯論（MAD）框架在一般推理方面顯示出顯著潛力，但其在高度結構化、知識密集的法律領域中的有效性仍然未被充分探索。在這項工作中，我們介紹了法律多代理辯論（L-MAD）框架，以系統地評估法律文本推理中的不同辯論結構和聚合方法。通過為多個代理分配不同的專家角色，L-MAD 在強大的單代理基準之上提高了多達 8\%。此外，分析辯論的擴展顯示出明顯的權衡：增加代理人數量會減少不一致性並提高準確性，而延長討論回合則會導致有害的 \textit{過度深思漂移}，使代理人強化彼此的錯誤。最終，我們的研究結果勾勒出在高風險法律推理環境中部署協作多代理系統的實際界限和安全邊際。
